## v1.33.0

Fixes the agent authoring contract: conditions, prompt types, the `var` tool and `{arg}` placeholders now match what the server does. One change can break code that relied on the old behavior (see "Behavior change").

### Added

- `var` tool type: `tools.var()` sets a thread variable that conditions and prompts can read from the next turn (#348)
- `{arg}` placeholders in `api` tool `request.url` and string values of an object `request.body` (#348)
- Prompt blocks accept `type` `custom`, `system` or `knowledge`, and an optional `condition`. New export `PROMPT_TYPES` (#348)
- Tools accept an optional `condition` (#348)
- `previewPrompt()` returns `conditionalKeys`, the blocks that apply only while their condition is true (#348)
- `intellectConfig.audit()` and `mgmt.doctor()` flag templated conditions: `skill_condition_template`, `tool_condition_template`, `prompt_bad_condition` (#348)
- `npm run live-verify:authoring`: live check of all of the above against a real account (#348)

### Behavior change

- A `condition` must be a bare expression such as `sys__avatar_enabled`. `{{ }}` and `{% %}` forms are rejected with `bad_request` before the write, because the server answers them with an empty reply (#348)
- An `api` tool with an undeclared `{name}` in the url, or literal braces in a string body, is rejected with `bad_placeholder` (#348)
- An unset `condition` is `null` on read. The SDK treats `null` as "no condition" everywhere (#348)

### Docs and skill

- New Conditions section, `var` tool, `{arg}` and shared-skills docs. Shared skills (`partner_id: 0`) show in `skills.list` and cannot be read with `skills.get` (#348, #355)
- All three prompt `type` values listed in one place (#353, #355)
- The app-builder skill has a hard rule for bare conditions and a new `skill-condition` eval (#348, #349)
- Contributor and user docs split and cleaned up (#333, #336, #337, #339, #341, #342, #344, #346)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/kaltura/intelligent-agents-sdk/compare/v1.32.0...v1.33.0
